To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the core-shell nanocomposite PU/Cs nanocomposite fibers were successfully fabricated at the optimal processing parameters and the core-shell structure was confirmed by SEM and TEM images.

core-shell PU/C nanofibers could be produced successfully at the optimized conditions and the results of characterization of these nanofibers showed that these nanofibres have potential to be used as a platform for the bio-active scaffolds in tissue-engineering.
the core-shell nanocomposites were successfully fabricated at the optimized processing parameters using electrospinning method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of the core-shell PU nanofibrous scaffold with the potential applications in the tissue engineering.
the preparation and characterization of the PU, Cs/PEO, and core-shell PU/ Cs/PEO nanofibers
the preparation, characterization and process optimization of core-shell PU/chitosan nanocomposite nanofibers using electrospinning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the core-shell nanocomposite nanofibers could be a potential candidate for the development of a novel three dimensional scaffolds for the tissue engineering applications.
the core-shell structure of PU/Cs nanoffibers can be considered as an appropriate platform for bioactive materials in tissue engineering.
the electrospun core-shell PU/Ce nanofibers with a high surface area, high mechanical strength and high porosity, can be used as an ideal platform for the bio-active scaffolds in tissue regeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the core-shell nanocomposite nanofibers could be produced at the optimized conditions using the electrospinning process and the inclusion of Cs to the shell did not affect the crystallinity and the thermal degradation of PU/Cs nanocomposite nanoffibers.
this work can be used to design the core-shell nanocomposite nanofibers for the potential applications in biomedical and pharmaceutical fields.

the inclusion of PEO to the shell of the core-shell nanocomposites, did not induce significant changes in the structure of the nanocomposite, however it improved the thermal stability and crystallinity of the nanofibrous structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the core-shell nanocomposites can be produced using the electrospinning technique and the core-shell nanomaterials can be used in the biomedical field.
we have demonstrated the possibility of using electrospinning for the production of PU/Cs core shell nanofibers and the possibility to use them as a potential platform in the tissue engineering.
the core-shell nanocomposite nanofibers with a PU/Cs core and a PEO/Cs shell can be produced at the optimum processing conditions using the electrospinning technique.
